source: the ice near the lens that is seen grain by grain: every grain is a body of its own on the orbit of its radius, at a height of its own above or below the middle of the plane, lit by the Sun. Lengths in planet radii, a size is the width of a grain. Read by ice.ts (how much of the sheet the grains carry) and grains.ts (the grains).
note: share: where the grains of the counted levels show whole, this share of the sheet's optical depth is grains (as far as the levels can carry it) and the rest stays a sheet in their shade. The grains are a part of the sheet: a cell of a level holds a grain where the sheet has depth, by the share of the sheet's depth over the depth all counted levels carry together, so the grains lie in the ringlets; a grain has the brightness the sheet has at its place, times one plus the cosine of the view over the cosine of the Sun for a grain in full light, and is in the shade of the grains above it by its height in the layer. So the grains and what is left of the sheet add up to the whole sheet, and where the grains go below a few pixels they hand over to it with no seam. bound: the cells of a row are looked at up to this many times the share its depth by the model asks for (the ringlets of the shader raise the depth above the model in places). soft: a grain at the limit of its share comes in over this share of it. foot: a grain reads the sheet with a footprint of this many of its widths, or the pixel's if that is larger. largestPoint: the largest point the renderer may be asked for, in pixels. capacity: the most grains of one take.

levels.note: per level: cell, the size of a cell across and along the orbit; layers, how many sets of rows lie in each other; presence, the share of the cells that may hold a grain; size, smallest and largest width, and power (the width is the smallest plus the span times a number of its own from 0 to 1 to this power); height, the grains float within this far above and below the middle of the plane, a few of them up to heightFar times as far; pixels, the level shows by the width on screen of its middle grain: none below the first number of pixels, whole from the second; reach, it fades out between these two distances from the lens; counted, 1 if the level is a part of the sheet's depth (see share), 0 if its pieces are ice of their own; bySheet, for a level that is not counted: the depth of the sheet at which it has its full presence; largest, a piece that would show wider than the first number of pixels fades out up to the second; white, how far its colour is white rather than the colour of the sheet there; gain, the factor on its brightness; lift, a grain of a counted level that shows whole is brighter by this share: the eye takes a field of bright and dark grains for darker than the same light spread evenly, and this keeps the level of the picture the same from the sheet into the grains.

pebbles
chunks

lobes.note: the shape of a grain: three balls that overlap, inside the grain's round outline, one near the middle and two further out. spread: how far from the middle the centres of the outer balls may lie, as a share of the grain's radius (they lie between half of that and all of it); first: the first ball lies within this share of that from the middle; radius: smallest and largest radius of a ball as a share of the grain's (no further out than the outline). pixels: a grain narrower than the first number of pixels is drawn as one ball of the same area, from the second its balls stand fully apart. tumble: how many times a grain turns about the line of sight while the orbit that keeps pace with the globe turns once, at most (each grain has its own rate, to either side).

light.note: how a grain is lit over its body: ambient, the light from the ice around it; wrap, how far the Sun's light reaches around the body (0: a hard edge of shade at a right angle to the Sun); through, the light that comes through the thin rim of a grain that is seen against the Sun; spread: a grain is brighter or darker than the ice at its place by up to this share. layer: the height of the layer the shade of grain on grain is counted in (a grain this far above the middle of the plane is in full light, one this far below has all counted grains above it).
